children: Shares of Enovix rose after the company said it received a purchase order for 100,000 drone battery units.
Shares were up 12% to $2.81 after Tuesday's bell, after closing down 3.1% at $2.51. Through the close, the stock had fallen 66% this year and hit a 52-week low of $2.40 last week.
The company said a multinational drone systems provider placed the order, with deliveries scheduled for the first half of next year.

The customer is expected to place follow-on orders beginning in the second half of next year, and Enovix said it expects additional pipeline opportunities to convert into purchase orders going forward.
"Drone makers need high-performance batteries from a qualified, non-Chinese source now, and this order shows Enovix can deliver," Chief Revenue Officer Steve Bakos said.
